1	# Reference lock
2	
3	**Load in Step 1b, for every tier.** Refero's research-first method, adapted to this
4	skill's four-tier gate (`SKILL.md` Step 2): Tier 0 locked · Tier 1 derive · Tier 2
5	reference · Tier 3 invent. The lock is not a Tier-2-only artifact — every tier states
6	one before Step 2 runs, because every tier is a claim about where the direction comes
7	from, and an unstated claim is how Tier 1 gets skipped in favour of invention.
8	
9	| | |
10	|---|---|
11	| **Reads** | The brief, Step 1 pre-flight findings, Step 2 tier evidence (`DESIGN.md`, brand assets, user URL/screenshot, or nothing), the design catalog, 21st.dev for tech/SaaS shots, Refero MCP when configured. |
12	| **Does** | Runs the research loop below, captures references as read images (never from memory), fills the reference-lock block and decision ledger, checks the build against anti-averaging and token/media-role preservation. |
13	| **Writes** | Nothing persisted by default — the lock is stated in-session, out loud, before Step 2 and Step 4. When the system is being locked to a portable file, its fields feed [`design-md.md`](design-md.md). |
14	| **Human checks** | Whether the named primary reference is actually the dominant voice in the build, not a label pasted over an averaged result — the one judgment this file cannot automate. |
15	
16	---
17	
18	## What changes per tier
19	
20	The loop is identical; only what plays the role of "the reference" changes.
21	
22	- **Tier 0 — locked.** Reconstructed, not invented: read `DESIGN.md` and what's
23	  already built from it, and write down what "preserve" means. Primary = the
24	  locked system itself.
25	- **Tier 1 — derive.** Primary = the brand evidence (logo, wordmark, hex, deployed
26	  site, `tailwind.config` colours). Borrowed details may come from competitor or
27	  category references; they extend the language, never re-set it.
28	- **Tier 2 — reference.** Primary = the user-supplied URL or screenshot. Refero's
29	  native case; the fields map straight across.
30	- **Tier 3 — invent.** Primary = the invented world's own bible
31	  ([`invention.md`](invention.md)) — locking against it stops the second component
32	  from drifting into a different invented world than the first.
33	
34	At every tier, a major visual choice with no source in the lock is not shipped.
35	
36	---
37	
38	## A brief is not a build target
39	
40	Refero states the rule this file exists to enforce, in one sentence: *"**A brief is not a
41	build target.** Before implementation, lock either a user-provided visual source, an
42	existing product/design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an explicit
43	reference-locked direction approved for direct build."*
44	
45	This is the sentence that closes the skip route. When the direction feels obvious and the
46	signature act is being built straight from the brief, the visual target still gets named
47	first — one line saying what this is being built *toward* and what must not drift:
48	
49	```text
50	Build target: [existing UI / user screenshot / URL capture / selected mockup / approved reference lock]
51	What must not drift: [canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density]
52	```
53	
54	If no target exists and the visual direction is material, explore options or get one
55	reference-locked direction approved. A build whose only stated source is the brief is a
56	build with no source at all.
57	
58	## Research loop
59	
60	Six angles, not one query:
61	
62	1. **Broad aesthetic** — the mood in plain language ("warm coastal Nordic hospitality").
63	2. **Domain / category** — what this business actually is.
64	3. **Known brand** — a specific strong player in the segment, named.
65	4. **Register** — the row from `SKILL.md`'s register table this brief lands in.
66	5. **Anti-reference** — one thing this build should *not* look like, sharpening the
67	   boundary the same way a rejected direction does in the lock block below.
68	6. **Cross-domain wildcard** — one reference from *outside* the category, chosen for a
69	   quality rather than a subject. *"A banking app can be inspired by a meditation app's
70	   calm."* Upstream's map:
71	
72	   | This brief's domain | Look at |
73	   |---|---|
74	   | Healthcare | Meditation apps (calm), fitness apps (motivation), journaling (reflection) |
75	   | Finance | Productivity tools (clarity), weather apps (data viz), news apps (hierarchy) |
76	   | Education | Games (engagement), music apps (progression), social apps (community) |
77	   | E-commerce | Editorial sites (storytelling), gallery apps (browsing), travel (discovery) |
78	   | Enterprise | Consumer apps (polish), design tools (power + clarity), docs (wayfinding) |
79	
80	   *"Don't force connections — but don't limit yourself to competitors either."* Competitors
81	   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
82	   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.
83	
84	**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
85	screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.
86	
87	Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
88	viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
89	turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
90	instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
91	were opened.
92	
93	**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**
94	
95	```text
96	What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
97	What to leave: [what does not apply here]
98	```
99	
100	*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
101	reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
102	"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
103	declarative.
104	
105	**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
106	section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
107	radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
108	asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
109	placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
110	carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
111	it looks nothing like.
112	
113	**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
114	Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
115	audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.
116	
117	From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
118	the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.
119	
120	**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
121	2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
122	it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.
123	
124	### Sources, in order
125	
126	1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
127	   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
128	   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
129	2. **Inspo MCP** (`mcp__inspo__*`), per [`inspo-mcp.md`](inspo-mcp.md) — the second
130	   source, right after the catalogue, when the catalogue lacks the page's form. The
131	   primary reference's tokens are fetched with `get_design_system`, never read off
132	   an image.
133	3. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
134	   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
135	4. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
136	   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
137	   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
138	5. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
139	   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
140	   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.
141	
142	### When the results are weak
143	
144	Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
145	ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
146	Weak):
147	
148	1. **Broaden the query.**
149	2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
150	   adjective too many.
151	3. **Search adjacent categories.**
152	4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
153	   describing a type.
154	5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.
155	
156	Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
157	stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.
158	
159	### Transcribe the category's live headlines
160	
161	Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
162	their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
163	what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
164	copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
165	[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
166	as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
167	during it.
168	
169	## The reference-lock block
170	
171	Verbatim fields, filled before any code:
172	
173	```text
174	Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
175	Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
176	Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
177	Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
178	Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
179	Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
180	Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
181	```
182	
183	**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
184	drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
185	a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.
186	
187	## Decision ledger
188	
189	Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:
190	
191	| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
192	|---|---|---|---|
193	| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
194	| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |
195	
196	**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
197	justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.
198	
199	**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
200	requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
201	interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —
202	including for the signature act itself, which is the row most often left blank on the
203	grounds that it is obvious. An example of a filled row from upstream's own worked case:
204	*"Memorable detail | 'Operational value' strip showing saved hours/cost by plan | Brief +
205	analytics product context | Metric strip as evidence, not decoration | Makes pricing feel
206	tied to outcome."*
207	
208	## The asset lock
209	
210	Written **before** anyone starts searching or generating — Step 5b has a pipeline but no
211	spec upstream of it, and an asset sourced without a spec is an asset chosen by whatever the
212	search returned. One block per media slot:
213	
214	```text
215	Asset role: [hero image / texture / illustration / thumbnail / cutout]
216	Slot: [dimensions / aspect ratio / location on the page]
217	Art direction: [source, palette, subject, rendering, crop, density]
218	Avoid: [wrong palette, extra text, brand drift, generic placeholders]
219	```
220	
221	The `Avoid` line is the one that earns its keep: it is the reject field applied to a single
222	asset, and it is what a QA pass compares the delivered frame against.
223	*"Generated assets must be placed into the implementation before handoff or documented as
224	blocked"* — never quietly downgraded to a gradient. That downgrade is the media-role drift
225	this file's next section already bans, caught one step earlier.
226	
227	---
228	
229	## Anti-averaging
230	
231	Choose a dominant direction. Secondary references contribute narrow, named details;
232	they do not get to soften the primary one. The failure mode is specific: a dark
233	workbench reference, an acid-yellow document site, and a serif editorial page do not
234	average into a warm cream canvas with muted clay accents — **dark + acid + serif is
235	not cream + orange + polite serif.** Dark → cream, saturated → muted clay, sharp →
236	rounded, distinctive layout → generic hero-and-sections: each swap is the
237	intersection eating the direction, not synthesis.
238	
239	Run these against the lock before shipping — ported from `anti-ai-slop.md`:
240	
241	- **Identity test.** If the first viewport could belong to any other company,
242	  branding lost to averaging. Add the one detail that makes this unmistakably *this*
243	  brand's build.
244	- **Editorial test.** If swapping the logo for a coffee shop, boutique hotel, or
245	  literary magazine still makes the hero feel plausible, the build has drifted into
246	  generic calm-editorial slop regardless of what the lock says on paper.
247	- **Screenshot test.** Would this pass next to real products in the named
248	  register, or does it read as the safe middle every other page also landed on?
249	
250	A lock that names a dominant primary and still fails these three was averaged during
251	implementation, not during research — check the built page against the lock's
252	"Reject" line specifically.
253	
254	## Token-role and media-role preservation
255	
256	**Token-role preservation.** A source's role for a colour, radius, shadow, or
257	component is part of the token, not separable from it. A CTA-only accent used as a
258	section background, a code-only syntax colour promoted to UI chrome, or a decorative
259	gradient turned into a core surface are all role drift. Preserve the role or drop
260	the token — never repurpose it to make a layout "work."
261	
262	**Media-role preservation.** An image-led reference never collapses to text-only
263	because the image was hard to produce. If the real asset genuinely is not
264	available, the placeholder must be honest, not silent:
265	
266	```text
267	Placeholder — [slot name]
268	Aspect: [ratio, e.g. 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile]
269	Art direction: [subject, lighting, crop the real asset will match]
270	Alt: [describes the intended real subject, not "placeholder image"]
271	```
272	
273	A placeholder with no aspect ratio, no art direction, and generic alt text is the
274	same failure as no image at all — it just fails one render cycle later.
275	
276	---
277	
278	## Three persona sketches
279	
280	`SKILL.md` Step 5 pass 12 and [`verbs/review.md`](verbs/review.md) § 4 both resolve ties
281	with "named personas". Nothing in the chain created any, so the tie-break pointed at an
282	artifact that did not exist. It does now, and it is three lines in `BRIEF.md` — not the
283	per-project persona documents upstream files away, which is a research deliverable this
284	chain has no room for.
285	
286	Select and write **three**, following upstream's proportions (*"2–3 primary users, 1–2 edge
287	case users, 1 stress case user"*), compressed to one line each:
288	
289	```text
290	Primary: [who they are] · [device and connection] · [what they came to do]
291	Edge:    [who sits at the margin] · [the ability or context that puts them there] · [what breaks first]
292	Stress:  [the same job under a named difficult circumstance] · [what they cannot afford to lose]
293	```
294	
295	**The conditions are situational, not only permanent.** Upstream's spectrum is explicit that
296	*"bright sunlight, noisy environment, one hand occupied, driving, multitasking, emotional
297	distress, unfamiliar language, slow connection"* belong beside vision, hearing, motor and
298	cognitive conditions. A stress persona on a Swedish harbour-restaurant page is a person on a
299	phone, outdoors, in sun, deciding where to eat in the next ten minutes — and that persona
300	decides more layout questions than any abstract one.
301	
302	**Write the intersections down.** *"A sighted user in bright sunlight has similar needs to a
303	low-vision user. A stressed parent holding a baby has similar motor constraints to someone
304	with limited hand mobility. A non-native speaker has similar needs to someone with a
305	cognitive processing difference."* Each intersection is a universal-design opportunity: one
306	fix that pays twice.
307	
308	**Then ask the one question that makes the set honest:** *"Which persona makes you most
309	uncomfortable?"* — *"that one probably needs the most attention."* Ask it of the brief, and
310	of the user when there is a user to ask. Discomfort is the signal that a persona was
311	included for completeness and is about to be designed around rather than for.
312	
313	Sketches that read as cardboard cutouts have failed. The check is upstream's own: *"do these
314	feel like real people, or cardboard cutouts?"*
315	
316	## Feeding Step 2 and Step 5
317	
318	**Into Step 2.** At **Tier 2**, the lock *is* the direction — its primary reference
319	sets the token commitments directly. At **Tiers 0–1**, the lock is the **quality
320	bar** the locked or derived system has to clear: the locked tokens still win on
321	value, but the captured references are what "as good as" means, concretely.
322	
323	**Into Step 5 visual QA.** Carry the lock's fields straight into the QA pass:
324	
325	```text
326	Source truth: [the reference lock, or the DESIGN.md it fed]
327	Implementation evidence: [local screenshot, deployed URL screenshot, captured app state]
328	Viewport/state: [desktop/mobile, route, theme, interaction state]
329	```
330	
331	Classify findings P0–P3 (broken/unreadable · major drift from the lock · moderate
332	mismatch or missing state · post-handoff polish). **No handoff with an open P0, P1,
333	or P2.** A P3 may ship with the finding named; P0–P2 block.
334	
335	## Worked example — Skärgårdskrogen (Swedish harbour restaurant, warm photographic)
336	
337	A harbourside restaurant on the Bohuslän coast. Register: **warm photographic**
338	(`SKILL.md` register table — harbour restaurant, guesthouse, tourism, family
339	business), with `klova/` as this skill's own in-repo worked example for the
340	register (`house-physics.md`).
341	
342	**Research loop:**
343	
344	1. Broad aesthetic — "warm coastal Nordic hospitality."
345	2. Domain/category — harbourside seafood dining, Bohuslän archipelago.
346	3. Known brand — a west-coast Swedish harbour restaurant with a photograph-led site.
347	4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
348	5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
349	   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.
350	
351	Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
352	and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.
353	
354	**Reference-lock block:**
355	
356	```text
357	Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
358	Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
359	Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
360	Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
361	Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
362	Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
363	Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
364	```
365	
366	**Decision ledger:**
367	
368	| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
369	|---|---|---|---|
370	| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
371	| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
372	| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
373	| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
374	| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |
375	
376	A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
377	`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker

379	dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.
380	
381	## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)
382	
383	- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
384	- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

# Reference lock

**Load in Step 1b, for every tier.** Refero's research-first method, adapted to this
skill's four-tier gate (`SKILL.md` Step 2): Tier 0 locked · Tier 1 derive · Tier 2
reference · Tier 3 invent. The lock is not a Tier-2-only artifact — every tier states
one before Step 2 runs, because every tier is a claim about where the direction comes
from, and an unstated claim is how Tier 1 gets skipped in favour of invention.

| | |
|---|---|
| **Reads** | The brief, Step 1 pre-flight findings, Step 2 tier evidence (`DESIGN.md`, brand assets, user URL/screenshot, or nothing), the design catalog, 21st.dev for tech/SaaS shots, Refero MCP when configured. |
| **Does** | Runs the research loop below, captures references as read images (never from memory), fills the reference-lock block and decision ledger, checks the build against anti-averaging and token/media-role preservation. |
| **Writes** | Nothing persisted by default — the lock is stated in-session, out loud, before Step 2 and Step 4. When the system is being locked to a portable file, its fields feed [`design-md.md`](design-md.md). |
| **Human checks** | Whether the named primary reference is actually the dominant voice in the build, not a label pasted over an averaged result — the one judgment this file cannot automate. |

---

## What changes per tier

The loop is identical; only what plays the role of "the reference" changes.

- **Tier 0 — locked.** Reconstructed, not invented: read `DESIGN.md` and what's
  already built from it, and write down what "preserve" means. Primary = the
  locked system itself.
- **Tier 1 — derive.** Primary = the brand evidence (logo, wordmark, hex, deployed
  site, `tailwind.config` colours). Borrowed details may come from competitor or
  category references; they extend the language, never re-set it.
- **Tier 2 — reference.** Primary = the user-supplied URL or screenshot. Refero's
  native case; the fields map straight across.
- **Tier 3 — invent.** Primary = the invented world's own bible
  ([`invention.md`](invention.md)) — locking against it stops the second component
  from drifting into a different invented world than the first.

At every tier, a major visual choice with no source in the lock is not shipped.

---

## A brief is not a build target

Refero states the rule this file exists to enforce, in one sentence: *"**A brief is not a
build target.** Before implementation, lock either a user-provided visual source, an
existing product/design-system target, a selected generated mockup, or an explicit
reference-locked direction approved for direct build."*

This is the sentence that closes the skip route. When the direction feels obvious and the
signature act is being built straight from the brief, the visual target still gets named
first — one line saying what this is being built *toward* and what must not drift:

```text
Build target: [existing UI / user screenshot / URL capture / selected mockup / approved reference lock]
What must not drift: [canvas, typography, accent roles, layout, media, density]
```

If no target exists and the visual direction is material, explore options or get one
reference-locked direction approved. A build whose only stated source is the brief is a
build with no source at all.

## Research loop

Six angles, not one query:

1. **Broad aesthetic** — the mood in plain language ("warm coastal Nordic hospitality").
2. **Domain / category** — what this business actually is.
3. **Known brand** — a specific strong player in the segment, named.
4. **Register** — the row from `SKILL.md`'s register table this brief lands in.
5. **Anti-reference** — one thing this build should *not* look like, sharpening the
   boundary the same way a rejected direction does in the lock block below.
6. **Cross-domain wildcard** — one reference from *outside* the category, chosen for a
   quality rather than a subject. *"A banking app can be inspired by a meditation app's
   calm."* Upstream's map:

   | This brief's domain | Look at |
   |---|---|
   | Healthcare | Meditation apps (calm), fitness apps (motivation), journaling (reflection) |
   | Finance | Productivity tools (clarity), weather apps (data viz), news apps (hierarchy) |
   | Education | Games (engagement), music apps (progression), social apps (community) |
   | E-commerce | Editorial sites (storytelling), gallery apps (browsing), travel (discovery) |
   | Enterprise | Consumer apps (polish), design tools (power + clarity), docs (wayfinding) |

   *"Don't force connections — but don't limit yourself to competitors either."* Competitors
   solve the same problem the same way, which is precisely how a category default becomes
   invisible. `select.py --wildcard` is the catalogue-side version of this angle.

**Quality over quantity: *"5 excellent references beat 20 mediocre ones."*** A wall of
screenshots is not research; it is deferred judgment. Curate down before capturing.

Then: **capture 3–4 full references as images and read them**, long pages in
viewport-sized slices. Memory returns wrong facts — two market-leading pages
turned out to *centre* their heroes, and one coloured words inside the headline
instead of switching typeface, opposite of what was assumed before the images
were opened.

**Every captured reference carries two lines, not one:**

```text
What to take: [the specific element or quality to learn from]
What to leave: [what does not apply here]
```

*"This prevents wholesale copying."* A reference with no lesson is decoration, and a
reference with only a "take" line is the one that quietly becomes the whole build. The
"leave" line is also what makes the primary/borrowed split below enforceable rather than
declarative.

**Extract more than colour and type.** From each reference, read out: layout system,
section rhythm and composition · card, button and surface treatments · borders, shadows,
radius · elevation and depth rules · imagery, graphic and illustration treatment · media
asset strategy (real asset, generated, code-native primitive, product screenshot, or
placeholder) · do and don't rules · **one memorable visual move to adapt**. A lock that
carries a palette and a typeface and nothing structural is why a build "referenced" a page
it looks nothing like.

**Give each source a bounded job.** *"Primary style: overall mood, density, and structure.
Secondary styles: specific borrowed details. User context: adapt everything to the product,
audience, and task."* A source with no job is a source that gets averaged.

From the 3–4 captured, pick **one primary** and take **1–2 borrowed details** from
the rest. Nothing else survives into the lock.

**Flag accessibility failures in the references themselves.** *"A beautiful reference with
2:1 contrast ratios is not inspiration — it's a cautionary tale."* Name it when you capture
it, so the trait does not travel into the lock as craft.

### Sources, in order

1. **The design catalog** — `~/anti-slop-design/design-catalogue/`,
   `python scripts/query.py --family … --register … --grammar …`. Query by the
   register named in `SKILL.md`'s table, not by vibe.
2. **Inspo MCP** (`mcp__inspo__*`), per [`inspo-mcp.md`](inspo-mcp.md) — the second
   source, right after the catalogue, when the catalogue lacks the page's form. The
   primary reference's tokens are fetched with `get_design_system`, never read off
   an image.
3. **User-supplied URL or screenshot** — Tier 2's native input; also valid at any
   tier as a borrowed-detail source.
4. **21st.dev** for tech/SaaS product shots — browse, screenshot, study the
   treatment; borrow the principle and rebuild it in the locked tokens, never paste
   a component with its own palette into a Tier 0–2 build.
5. **Refero MCP**, if configured — `refero_search_styles` → `refero_get_style`.
   Optional. State plainly when it is not configured rather than silently skipping
   it; do not treat its absence as license to skip the research loop itself.

### When the results are weak

Sparse or generic results are a query problem before they are a source problem. Climb this
ladder before concluding the catalogue has nothing (Refero `mcp-tools.md` § If Results Are
Weak):

1. **Broaden the query.**
2. **Remove extra adjectives or constraints.** Two adjectives and a register is usually one
   adjective too many.
3. **Search adjacent categories.**
4. **Try a known-product or best-brand query.** Name a specific strong player instead of
   describing a type.
5. **Inspect later pages.** The first page of any index is the most averaged part of it.

Only after all five is "no usable reference in this register" a finding — and then it is
stated in the lock, not silently converted into invention.

### Transcribe the category's live headlines

Before writing a word of copy, read the **five best live pages in the category and quote
their headlines verbatim** into the lock. *"The bar is what the reader has already seen, not
what sounds nice in isolation"* (`upstream/slopmonster/references/sources.md`). Five lines,
copied exactly, with the source named. They belong here rather than in
[`copy-gate.md`](copy-gate.md) because they are a *reference* capture: the same discipline
as the four screenshots, applied to language, and read before the copy pass rather than
during it.

## The reference-lock block

Verbatim fields, filled before any code:

```text
Primary reference/direction: [one dominant source, named]
Preserve: [3-5 traits that must survive: canvas, type, accent, layout, density, media]
Borrow only: [1-2 specific secondary details]
Role rules: [source token/component meanings to preserve — CTA-only, code-only, decorative-only]
Media strategy: [photo:unsplash | photo:pexels | product surface | drawn system | generated | placeholder]
Reject: [defaults/averages that would collapse the direction]
Token commitments: [canvas, type, accent, radius, border/shadow, imagery — each with its role]
```

**Media strategy is an enum, not prose.** Pick exactly one value per media slot so
drift is visible at a glance: a hero declared `photo:unsplash` that quietly becomes
a CSS gradient is a caught regression; a hero declared "some kind of photo" is not.

Every entry in the lock traces back through this table:

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| [palette / type / layout / media choice] | [reference / catalog query / brand asset / craft rule] | [token or component role to preserve] | [reason specific to this brief] |
| **Memorable detail** | [the reference the move was adapted from] | [what the move does on this page] | [why *this* brief earns it] |

**A major visual choice with no row here is not shipped.** Not "shipped and
justified after" — the row exists before the choice does.

**The `Memorable detail` row is mandatory, and the rule applies to it too.** Refero's
requirement is unambiguous: *"Create at least one memorable detail: a visual move,
interaction, layout choice, or copy detail users would remember."* No row, not shipped —

4. Register — warm photographic, per the table above; cross-check against `klova/`.
5. Anti-reference — the editorial-print register (`calyx.html`): its apparatus on a
   family harbour restaurant reads as pretension, not craft.

Four captured and read: `klova/` itself, two competitor harbour-restaurant sites,
and `calyx.html` as the anti-reference boundary check.

**Reference-lock block:**

```text
Primary reference/direction: klova/ — centred logo lockup over full-bleed harbour photography, no rail, no kicker, no edition marker.
Preserve: centred logo lockup with no rail; full-bleed hero photograph with generous framing air on secondary images; one real outlined button sized to be pressed; warm serif display at conversational (not oversized-drop-cap) scale; dark-navy footer as the page's one tonal inversion.
Borrow only: dotted carousel indicator for the food gallery (competitor B — klova/ has no gallery, so this is a genuinely new need, not a style import); 12px rounded image corners (competitor B).
Role rules: the outlined button is CTA-only, never a secondary link style; the navy footer tone is inversion-only, never a section background elsewhere on the page.
Media strategy: photo:unsplash, sourced and vendored per photo-sources.md until real restaurant photography is supplied; hero 16:9 desktop / 4:3 mobile, framed with 24-48px air — never full-bleed-with-type-over, the editorial-print move this build explicitly rejects.
Reject: kicker microformat, grain film, ledger pricing, edition markers, italic serif drop caps — all editorial-print apparatus a family harbour restaurant cannot plausibly publish.
Token commitments: warm ivory canvas; near-black ink; one terracotta accent used only on the button and one wordmark word (never as fill); slate captions with a separate, measured value for the dark footer ground.
```

**Decision ledger:**

| Decision | Source | Source rule/role | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| Warm photographic, not editorial print | `SKILL.md` register table + anti-reference read of `calyx.html` | register selects apparatus | Family-run harbour restaurant, not a publishing entity |
| Centred logo lockup, no rail | `klova/` (primary) | layout role: identity-first hero | The photograph is the primary hire, not editorial structure |
| Real outlined button | `klova/` (primary) | CTA-only | Warm-photographic register expects a pressable button, unlike print/cinematic typeset links |
| Dotted carousel for gallery | Competitor B (borrowed) | gallery navigation only | `klova/` had no gallery; licensed as one named borrowed detail, not a wholesale style import |
| One terracotta accent, display-scale only | `house-physics.md` structural rule | accent role: CTA + display, never fill | Prevents the accent diluting into a second colour system |

A rejected direction here would average `klova/`'s warm photographic register with
`calyx.html`'s editorial apparatus into a soft-cream page with a restrained kicker
and a half-outlined button that is neither a typeset link nor a real one — the
dark+acid+serif-vs-cream+orange+polite-serif failure, in miniature.

## Two additions from the 2026-09-03 A/B run (AB05)

- **A colour-swapped word in a headline is a gate-89 signal even without a serif.** "Se *exakt* vad som ändrades" with *exakt* in the accent is the same reflex as the italic word swap; use it only when a locked reference does it and the word carries the claim.
- **Token commitments name the anatomy of every priced or listed surface.** Write `pricing: ledger (hairline rows, display numerals)` or `features: label-rail`, so the lock carries house physics into Step 4 instead of falling back to bordered cards.

26	## Why it works
27	
28	Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens, confirmed by the
29	live capture. Taupe paper `#ada59b` is not a "canvas colour" in the usual
30	sense — it is the entire site: the source states no section ever changes
31	background, so there is no light/dark alternation, no card surface, nothing
32	but one monolithic warm gray that every element floats on directly. Because
33	white, off-white and near-black are all explicitly forbidden as backgrounds,
34	photography becomes the only source of colour or contrast variation on the
35	whole page.
36	
37	Typography stays deliberately tiny across every functional role — 11-13px
38	WorkSans for navigation, labels, and body, with an explicit rule against ever
39	scaling up "for a primary label." That restraint is what makes the one
40	exception, the SilkSerif wordmark at 23px with letter-spacing opened to
41	0.5-0.8em, read as a masthead rather than a logo: the letters are so widely
42	tracked they nearly detach from each other, and because nothing else on the
43	page is set in serif, that single word instantly reads as the title plate of
44	a magazine.
45	
46	The image field is the structural centrepiece: photographs are placed with
47	irregular margin offsets (101-209px) rather than on a grid, so the layout
48	reads as a scattered contact sheet, not a portfolio grid. A working
49	LINEAR/RANDOM toggle — the only rounded (9999px) element in the entire
50	system — lets a viewer switch between an ordered and a scattered arrangement
51	of the same images, making the "contact sheet" metaphor an actual, operable
52	feature rather than just a visual style. Note: the designlang extract flags a
53	red `#dc3545` (31 uses, Bootstrap's default "danger" hue) not present in the
54	captured screenshot or documented anywhere in the source — most plausibly an
55	incidental form-validation or "sold out"-style state colour triggered during
56	the crawl rather than a deliberate brand accent, so it is not added to the
57	palette above; the exact taupe hex also reads slightly differently live
58	(`#e5ddc4`, `#a2a093`) than in the captured tokens, consistent with warm-gray
59	sampling variance rather than a different brand colour.
60	
61	## What to borrow (principle)
62	
63	- **Make the canvas a single, unchanging surface across the entire site.**
64	  Refusing section-to-section colour changes forces every other design
65	  decision (spacing, scatter, photography) to carry the visual rhythm
66	  instead.
67	- **Cap UI text size with an explicit rule, not just a habit.** "Never scale
68	  up for a primary label" keeps a whisper-small system from eroding under
69	  the pressure to make one thing "important."
70	- **Reserve the one rounded shape for exactly one interactive feature.**
71	  A 9999px pill appearing only on a working layout toggle — nowhere else —
72	  makes that single curve meaningful rather than decorative.
73	- **Offer a genuinely operable metaphor, not just a visual one.** A real
74	  LINEAR/RANDOM toggle that rearranges the same photographs turns "contact
75	  sheet" from a style reference into an interactive feature.
76	- **Open tracking on a masthead word until letters nearly detach.** Extreme
77	  positive letter-spacing (0.5-0.8em) on a short serif word is what makes a
78	  wordmark read as a printed title rather than a typed logo.
79	
80	## What to leave
81	
82	- A monolithic single-colour canvas with zero section variation is a
83	  demanding constraint — any content type that needs visual separation (a
84	  pricing table, a form) has no built-in surface-shift tool to reach for.
85	- Irregular image offsets (101-209px, scattered) require genuine art
86	  direction per breakpoint; a naive responsive collapse would either overlap
87	  badly or lose the contact-sheet read entirely.
88	- Zero accent colour anywhere means the system offers no built-in way to
89	  signal state (hover beyond a colour swap to pure ink, active, error)
90	  without inventing a convention from scratch.
91	
92	## Signature move
93	
94	The LINEAR/RANDOM layout toggle: a stroke-only pill switch that rearranges
95	the same scattered photographs between an ordered and a randomized
96	composition — the only rounded, only interactive-feeling component on the
97	entire site, and the one place the "contact sheet" concept becomes literally
98	operable.
99	
100	## Motion
101	
102	(from designlang extract) Feel reads as mixed, and the page is scroll-linked.
103	Four durations are confirmed — 200ms, 300ms, 1s and a notably slow 2s — though
104	no easing curve is confidently identified (no dominant named family
105	registers). That wide spread, especially the 2s outlier, fits a genuinely
106	deliberate grid-rearrange animation: images repositioning across the scattered
107	field when the LINEAR/RANDOM toggle fires would plausibly need a slower,
108	choreographed duration rather than a snap cut. No keyframes are confirmed
109	firing. (observed in capture) the live capture confirms the scattered,
110	irregularly-offset image field and the LINEAR/RANDOM toggle are present and
111	match the described layout.
112	
113	| Token | Value | Easing |
114	|---|---|---|
115	| sm | 200ms | — |
116	| md | 300ms | — |
117	| xl | 1s | — |
118	| xxl (toggle rearrange) | 2s | — |
119	
120	## Brief
121	
122	Build a Copenhagen-style creative-studio portfolio with a single unchanging
123	canvas. Set the entire page on warm taupe `#ada59b` — no section, card, or
124	component ever uses a different background; white, off-white and near-black
125	are all forbidden as surfaces. Cap all UI text (nav, labels, body, metadata)
126	at 11-13px WorkSans Regular — never scale up for emphasis. Set the studio
127	name in a light serif at 23px with letter-spacing opened to 0.5-0.8em, tight
128	0.94 leading, centred in the top bar as the only serif moment on the site.
129	Arrange 6-8 photographs in an asymmetric scattered field with irregular
130	margin offsets (roughly 100-210px), each at 0px radius with no border or
131	shadow, ringed by floating uppercase category labels positioned at irregular
132	coordinates (top-left, top-centre, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-centre,
133	bottom-right). Add a working LINEAR/RANDOM toggle — a stroke-only 9999px
134	pill with a small circular thumb, the only rounded element anywhere — that
135	rearranges the image field between ordered and scattered layouts. Centre a
136	single studio-statement paragraph below at 13px with generous (180px) top
137	padding. No accent colour, no shadows, no elevation anywhere.
138

142	on-table or portrait-detail shots at high resolution, warm and slightly
143	desaturated, lit naturally rather than in a studio, cropped tight at varying
144	aspect ratios (1:1, 4:5, 3:2) so the collection reads as a contact sheet
145	rather than a uniform grid.
146

149	Unsplash first, Pexels second.

151	- "interior photography natural light desaturated"
152	- "packaging design close up studio"
153	- "portrait detail natural light editorial"

172	photography at varying tight crops; no illustration, no icons beyond fine
173	line-art strokes.
174	Reject: any second background colour; box-shadow or gradient; radius above
175	0px outside the toggle and rare small inset frames; a display weight above
176	Light/Regular; a centred multi-column body layout.
177	Token commitments: bg `#ada59b`, ink `#000000`, nav-text `#252525`,

26	## Why it works
27	
28	Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens. The studio's own UI stays
29	97% achromatic — ink black `#111118` and paper white carry almost everything — which
30	means the one place colour is allowed to exist, the work itself, reads as maximally
31	vivid by contrast. Capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius, practically a
32	lozenge) bleed whatever client palette they carry straight onto the cream page, so
33	the portfolio grid becomes a controlled burst of colour inside an otherwise
34	disciplined frame.
35	
36	Type does the same restraint-then-release move as the page's colour: PP Mori
37	carries every functional voice (nav, labels, body) at weights 200-600 with an
38	unusually wide 0.107em tracking on small sizes, while Editorial New — a didone
39	serif at weight 200 only — is reserved exclusively for display headlines from 48px
40	up to 160px. Because the thin serif never appears below 48px and the sans never
41	carries a display headline, the pairing reads as two distinct instruments rather
42	than a font stack.
43	
44	The single dramatic gesture is saved for the end: the entire page is light until
45	the footer, which inverts to `#111118` and is the only place the highlighter-yellow
46	`#fef199` accent appears — outlining a massive pill CTA. Holding one colour and one
47	inversion in reserve for the close makes the last screen feel like a different room,
48	not a louder button.
49	
50	## What to borrow (principle)
51	
52	- **Let client/project colour be the only colour.** A near-achromatic studio UI
53	  makes a portfolio grid read as more vivid, not less, because nothing competes
54	  with it.
55	- **Reserve an accent for exactly one section.** Saving a colour for the footer
56	  alone turns the close into an event instead of diluting the accent everywhere.
57	- **Pair one ultra-thin display face with one workhorse sans, never at the same
58	  size.** A 200-weight serif above 48px against a 200-600 weight sans below it
59	  keeps the tension legible instead of muddy.
60	- **Use one dramatic shape as a signature, sparingly.** An 800px "capsule" image
61	  radius reads as a device precisely because nothing else on the page shares it.
62	- **Track out small type generously.** 0.107em letter-spacing at 12-15px is what
63	  makes nav and labels read as fashion-editorial rather than default UI.
64	
65	## What to leave
66	
67	- The "Don't" list is empty in the source export — the system's constraints are
68	  implicit in its Do's, which makes fidelity harder to check without the live site.
69	- An 800px capsule radius depends on generous card width; at narrow/mobile
70	  breakpoints it will collapse toward a pill or a circle, losing the lozenge shape.
71	- A single reserved accent colour for one section only works if that section is
72	  genuinely the page's close — used mid-page it would read as an unexplained
73	  one-off.

75	## Signature move
76	
77	The circular rotating text badge — "AVAILABLE NOW" set on an invisible circle,
78	used once as a floating decorative element beside the hero headline rather than as
79	a repeatable component. It is deliberately not part of the design system; it is a
80	single ornament.

83

85	Interactive transitions run on a plain `ease` curve at three short durations —
86	100ms, 200ms and 300ms — the fastest tier for hover/colour changes, the slowest for
87	larger reveals; the broader transition log adds a 400ms opacity fade for section
88	entrances. The one keyframe confirmed in use is `slide`, a slide-x transform (3
89	uses) driving translateX motion — most likely the capsule-tile image slider/marquee
90	behaviour rather than the rotating text badge, since no rotate keyframe registers
91	as in-use (a `spin` keyframe exists in the stylesheet but isn't confirmed firing).
92	(observed in capture) the capsule-shaped image containers and the circular rotating
93	badge suggest the badge text itself may continuously rotate, and hover states on
94	ghost/filled pill buttons likely invert fill and text colour rather than adding
95	movement — consistent with the flat, shadow-free, editorial register of the rest of
96	the system.

107	Build a visual-design-studio portfolio. Canvas is paper white, ink is near-black

109	UI stays achromatic except for the highlighter-yellow `#fef199` reserved for the
110	footer only. Open on a full-width Editorial New weight-200 headline (48-160px,
111	line-height 1.0, no uppercase) stating the studio's promise in one or two lines.
112	Below, lay out a portfolio grid of capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius,
113	8px on the outer card) bleeding full client-project colour and imagery. Use PP Mori
114	at 0.107em tracking for all nav, labels and body copy; reserve 24px pill radius for

## Why it works

Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens. The studio's own UI stays
97% achromatic — ink black `#111118` and paper white carry almost everything — which
means the one place colour is allowed to exist, the work itself, reads as maximally
vivid by contrast. Capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius, practically a
lozenge) bleed whatever client palette they carry straight onto the cream page, so
the portfolio grid becomes a controlled burst of colour inside an otherwise
disciplined frame.

Type does the same restraint-then-release move as the page's colour: PP Mori
carries every functional voice (nav, labels, body) at weights 200-600 with an
unusually wide 0.107em tracking on small sizes, while Editorial New — a didone
serif at weight 200 only — is reserved exclusively for display headlines from 48px
up to 160px. Because the thin serif never appears below 48px and the sans never
carries a display headline, the pairing reads as two distinct instruments rather
than a font stack.

The single dramatic gesture is saved for the end: the entire page is light until
the footer, which inverts to `#111118` and is the only place the highlighter-yellow
`#fef199` accent appears — outlining a massive pill CTA. Holding one colour and one
inversion in reserve for the close makes the last screen feel like a different room,
not a louder button.

## What to borrow (principle)

- **Let client/project colour be the only colour.** A near-achromatic studio UI
  makes a portfolio grid read as more vivid, not less, because nothing competes
  with it.
- **Reserve an accent for exactly one section.** Saving a colour for the footer
  alone turns the close into an event instead of diluting the accent everywhere.
- **Pair one ultra-thin display face with one workhorse sans, never at the same
  size.** A 200-weight serif above 48px against a 200-600 weight sans below it
  keeps the tension legible instead of muddy.
- **Use one dramatic shape as a signature, sparingly.** An 800px "capsule" image
  radius reads as a device precisely because nothing else on the page shares it.
- **Track out small type generously.** 0.107em letter-spacing at 12-15px is what
  makes nav and labels read as fashion-editorial rather than default UI.

## What to leave

- The "Don't" list is empty in the source export — the system's constraints are
  implicit in its Do's, which makes fidelity harder to check without the live site.
- An 800px capsule radius depends on generous card width; at narrow/mobile
  breakpoints it will collapse toward a pill or a circle, losing the lozenge shape.
- A single reserved accent colour for one section only works if that section is
  genuinely the page's close — used mid-page it would read as an unexplained
  one-off.

## Signature move

The circular rotating text badge — "AVAILABLE NOW" set on an invisible circle,
used once as a floating decorative element beside the hero headline rather than as
a repeatable component. It is deliberately not part of the design system; it is a
single ornament.

## Motion

(from designlang extract) Feel reads as smooth, and the page is scroll-linked.
Interactive transitions run on a plain `ease` curve at three short durations —
100ms, 200ms and 300ms — the fastest tier for hover/colour changes, the slowest for
larger reveals; the broader transition log adds a 400ms opacity fade for section
entrances. The one keyframe confirmed in use is `slide`, a slide-x transform (3
uses) driving translateX motion — most likely the capsule-tile image slider/marquee
behaviour rather than the rotating text badge, since no rotate keyframe registers
as in-use (a `spin` keyframe exists in the stylesheet but isn't confirmed firing).
(observed in capture) the capsule-shaped image containers and the circular rotating
badge suggest the badge text itself may continuously rotate, and hover states on
ghost/filled pill buttons likely invert fill and text colour rather than adding
movement — consistent with the flat, shadow-free, editorial register of the rest of
the system.

|---|---|---|
| xs | 100ms | `ease` |
| sm | 200ms | `ease` |
| md | 300ms | `ease` |
| slide keyframe | — | translateX, 3 uses |

## Brief

Build a visual-design-studio portfolio. Canvas is paper white, ink is near-black
`#111118`, with soft-ash and stone-gray for muted borders and dividers — the whole
UI stays achromatic except for the highlighter-yellow `#fef199` reserved for the
footer only. Open on a full-width Editorial New weight-200 headline (48-160px,
line-height 1.0, no uppercase) stating the studio's promise in one or two lines.
Below, lay out a portfolio grid of capsule-shaped project tiles (800px radius,
8px on the outer card) bleeding full client-project colour and imagery. Use PP Mori
at 0.107em tracking for all nav, labels and body copy; reserve 24px pill radius for
buttons and 8px for cards and links. Add one floating circular rotating text badge
near the hero as a one-off ornament. Close on a full-width `#111118` inverted
footer panel with a giant 150px-radius CTA pill outlined in highlighter yellow.

## Image recipe

Not applicable as a primary photographic recipe — the site's imagery is client
project work (screenshots, illustration, branded colour blocks) rather than
photography. Where a portrait or process shot is needed: a plain, evenly lit studio
headshot or workspace detail of [SUBJECT], neutral background, no heavy retouching,
consistent with an achromatic UI that lets the subject's own colour read clean.

## Photo search

Unsplash first, Pexels second.
- "designer workspace desk minimal flat lay"
- "portrait studio lighting neutral background"
- "laptop screen mockup UI design work"
- "colour palette swatches paper minimal"

## Reference lock

Primary reference/direction: André Cândido — near-monochrome editorial portfolio,
whisper-thin didone display, colour reserved for client work and one footer accent.
Preserve (3-5 traits): 97% achromatic UI (`#111118` ink on white); Editorial New
weight 200 exclusively for display headlines 48px and above, never smaller, never
heavier; PP Mori at 0.107em tracking for all functional text; 800px capsule radius
on portfolio images vs. 8px on cards and 24px on buttons; a single dark `#111118`
footer inversion where highlighter yellow `#fef199` appears for the first and only
time.
Borrow only (1-2): the circular rotating "AVAILABLE NOW" text badge; the 150px-
radius oversized footer CTA pill.
Role rules: yellow never appears outside the footer panel; serif never carries body
copy or UI labels; sans never sets a display headline; client-project colour is the
only large colour field permitted pre-footer.
Media strategy: none (no external photography) — client-work screenshots and
colour blocks carry all chromatic content; any supplementary photography stays
neutral and desaturated to match the UI.
Reject: a second accent colour anywhere outside the footer; rounded corners below
8px or above 24px except the 800px image capsule; shadows or elevation; a bolded
Editorial New headline.
Token commitments: bg `#ffffff`, ink `#111118`, border `#dddddd`/`#bdbdbd`, muted
text `#7c7c7c`, footer accent `#fef199`; display weight 200 at 48-160px/leading 1.0;
body PP Mori 200-600 at 12-24px, 0.107em tracking on 12-15px sizes; radius 8px
cards, 24px buttons, 800px images, 150px footer CTA; base spacing unit 8px, section
gap 80-120px.

26	## Why it works
27	
28	Palette and type are read from Refero's extracted tokens, confirmed by the live
29	capture. The system has no accent colour at all — butter cream `#f9e5b1`, ink
30	black `#1d1e21`, warm bone and ash gray carry the entire page. That absence is
31	itself the brand signal: a venture firm's site with no "brand blue" reads as more
32	considered, not less finished, because every visual decision is forced onto type,
33	scale and whitespace instead of a swatch.
34	
35	A single typeface, Lausanne, runs the whole system at exactly three weights —
36	400 for body and nav, 600 for subheadings and button labels, 700 reserved
37	strictly for headlines 28px and above, capped at a 72px ceiling. Letter-spacing
38	follows classical convention rather than a flat value: it tightens at display
39	size and opens slightly at small body sizes, which is what keeps a single-family
40	system from feeling monotonous across six size steps.

.sr-only{position:absolute;width:1px;height:1px;padding:0;margin:-1px;overflow:hidden;clip:rect(0,0,0,0);white-space:nowrap;border:0;}

.headline-50{font-size:var(--headline-50);line-height:.8;letter-spacing:-.04em;font-weight:500;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- topline */
.topline{

}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- hero */
/* R3: the fixed 190svh CSS-sticky stage is gone. The pin distance is now
   owned by ScrollTrigger's own pinSpacing (desktop matchMedia branch,
   RORELSE-SPEC.md §2); hero-wrap just needs to size to its content so a
   no-JS/pre-JS view still shows one full stage, not a dead 90svh gap. */
.hero-wrap{position:relative;max-width:1440px;margin:0 auto;}
.hero-stage{

@media (max-width:767px){

  .hero-wrap{height:auto;}

.hero-cell{position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.hero-ov{background:var(--paper);display:flex;align-items:flex-end;padding:var(--cellpad);}
.hero-oh{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nv{background:var(--grey);}
.hero-nh{background:var(--mint);}
.hero-h1{max-width:14ch;}

.dither-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.color-layer{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}

/* card: a physical object (light stock, ink edge, hard offset shadow) so
   it reads against a black cell instead of disappearing into it. ~1.6x
   the R1 size at 1440 (was ~340px wide, now ~520px), 85:55 kept. */

  position:absolute;left:75%;top:50%;
  width:min(36vw,520px);
  aspect-ratio:85/55;
  transform:translate(-50%,-50%);

.card-flip{
  width:100%;height:100%;position:relative;
  transform-style:preserve-3d;

.face{
  position:absolute;inset:0;

  backface-visibility:hidden;

   that is a photo edge-to-edge reads as "the photo", not as "a light
   stock object sitting on the cell" - the mat is what makes the white
   stock actually visible against a black ÖH ground. */
.face--front{background:#fff;padding:6%;}
/* R6 bugfix: kontakt's front is a <button> wrapping <span>s (spans, unlike
   hero's <div>s, default to display:inline) - an inline, merely
   position:relative .photo never gets a real box (width/height are ignored
   on non-replaced inline elements), so it collapsed to a ~2px sliver and
   the absolutely-positioned img inside inherited that zero-size containing
   block. display:block here makes both tags behave identically. */
.face--front .photo{display:block;position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.5);}

.mark-dock{position:absolute;top:9%;left:9%;width:14%;z-index:2;}
.mark-dock svg{width:100%;height:auto;fill:#fff;filter:drop-shadow(0 0 3px rgba(0,0,0,.7));}
.card-mark{font-size:clamp(20px,2.6vw,32px);letter-spacing:-.02em;margin:0;}
.card-kicker{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(11px,1.1vw,14px);opacity:.65;margin:2px 0 0;}
.card-rule{border:0;border-top:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.25);margin:6px 0;width:100%;}
.card-services{display:flex;gap:10px;font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:clamp(10px,1.1vw,13px);}
.card-cta{font-size:clamp(13px,1.5vw,18px);text-decoration:underline;margin-top:4px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- tes */
.tes-top{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*2) var(--cellpad);}
.tes-top .headline-50{max-width:22ch;}
.tes-lower{min-height:104svh;}
.tes-stack{display:grid;grid-template-rows:repeat(3,1fr);gap:1px;background:#000;}
.tes-line{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;align-items:center;}
.tes-image{padding:0;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- process */
.process-row{}
.process-left{background:var(--grey);}
.process-sticky{position:sticky;top:calc(48px + var(--cellpad));}
.process-kicker{margin-bottom:14px;}
.process-title{margin:0 0 18px;max-width:11ch;}
.process-lock{max-width:32ch;opacity:.8;}
.process-image{position:relative;margin-top:32px;aspect-ratio:1/1;width:100%;max-width:680px;border:1px solid #000;overflow:hidden;}
.process-right{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);padding:0;}
.process-steps{list-style:none;}
.process-row-item{display:grid;grid-template-columns:56px 1fr;gap:14px;padding:22px var(--cellpad);border-top:1px solid #000;}
.process-row-item:first-child{border-top:none;}
.process-num{font-family:"Geist Mono";font-weight:400;font-size:13px;padding-top:4px;}
.process-step-title{margin:0 0 6px;}
.process-p{color:#bdbdbd;max-width:56ch;font-size:15px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- exempelcase */
/* R5 §A bugfix: 0.6x bottom padding (12px) was less than the SplitText
   mask-breathe allowance (0.16em, ~16-20px at this clamp size) needs to
   clear the word's own descenders before the cell's overflow:hidden edge
   - verify_motion.py's legibility scan caught the word's rendered box
   (with its mask wrapper's padding-bottom) genuinely sitting a few px
   below the cell's clip boundary at every scroll position (0vh visible,
   not >=40vh). Matching the top padding removes the clip entirely. */
.case-word-cell{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4 + 4px);overflow:hidden;}
.case-word-cell .headline-50{max-width:100%;}

.case-picker-cell{padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.2);background:#000;}
.case-picker{display:grid;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.case-choice{
  display:block;width:100%;margin:0;padding:0;border:0;background:var(--paper);color:inherit;
  font:inherit;text-align:left;cursor:pointer;-webkit-appearance:none;appearance:none;
}
.case-choice-frame{position:relative;display:block;aspect-ratio:16/10;overflow:hidden;background:var(--grey);}
.case-choice-frame img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;transform:scale(1);transition:transform .7s cubic-bezier(.23,1,.32,1);will-change:transform;}
@media (hover:hover){
  .case-choice:hover .case-choice-frame img,
  .case-choice:focus-visible .case-choice-frame img{transform:scale(1.04);}
}
.case-choice:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--mint);outline-offset:-2px;}
.case-choice-meta{display:block;padding:16px var(--cellpad) 20px;border-bottom:4px solid transparent;}
.case-choice[aria-pressed="true"] .case-choice-meta{border-bottom-color:var(--mint);}
.case-choice-meta .h3{display:block;margin-bottom:4px;font-size:22px;}

/* ------------------------------------------------------------- showcase (B2/C) */
.showcase-stage{display:grid;grid-template-columns:1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
@media (min-width:768px){ .showcase-stage{grid-template-columns:7fr 5fr;} }
.showcase-embed-cell{padding:0;background:var(--paper);position:relative;overflow:hidden;}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-frame-wrap{position:relative;width:100%;height:100%;overflow:hidden;background:var(--paper);}
.showcase-embed-cell .showcase-poster{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:cover;}
.showcase-embed-cell iframe{
  position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:1440px;height:900px;border:0;background:var(--paper);
  transform-origin:top left;pointer-events:none;opacity:0;
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  .showcase-embed-cell{position:sticky;top:48px;height:56svh;z-index:2;}
}
@media (min-width:768px){
  /* R6 §3, two stacked causes, both fixed here:
     1) .showcase-side's natural content (all 5/6 rows, R5's rise-mask kept
        every body visible at once) was taller than the embed cell's
        explicit height. A CSS grid item with an explicit height does not
        stretch to match a taller sibling's row track - the TRACK grows to
        fit the tall side instead, leaving the embed cell short of the
        row's actual height by the difference (measured ~110px), exposing
        the stage's own black gap background below the frame. Pinning both
        columns to the SAME explicit height (with the side's own
        overflow-y:auto as a never-clip safety net) makes them structurally
        impossible to mismatch, regardless of how much text a future edit
        adds.
     2) That explicit height was `100svh - 48px`, sized to sit BELOW the
        48px sticky topline - but the pin (`start:'top top'`) puts the
        section's rendered top at the viewport's own y:0, with the topline
        merely painted on top of (not offsetting) its first 48px. The
        result: content correctly avoids the topline visually, but then
        runs 48px short of the viewport's bottom edge, showing the stage's
        black background as a trailing band under both columns (measured:
        embed/side bottom at 852 of a 900-tall viewport). Hero's own pin
        has this identical 48px arithmetic and gap - invisible there only
        because it lands on the page's own black background either side.
        Showcase's is visible because there's real content flush above it.
        Fixed the same way hero's is invisible: fill the FULL viewport
        (100svh) - the topline still visually covers the top 48px (it's
        position:sticky, z-index:40, opaque), but the bottom now lands
        exactly on the viewport edge, so no gap is left to expose.

     R7 runda 2, fynd 1: that "topline merely painted on top" claim was
     wrong for `.showcase-head`'s own rubrik - the topline IS opaque and
     DOES cover whatever renders in its first 48px; it just happened not to
     matter for hero (dark ground either side). Here `.showcase-head`'s
     headline-40 sits flush at the pinned section's very top edge, so its
     cap-height rendered UNDER the topline and got visually sheared (lead's
     through-05..through-12, 2026-09-25). Fix: pin the section 48px lower
     instead of hiding 48px under an opaque bar - `start:'top top+=48'` on
     the ScrollTrigger (setupDesktopEngine) puts the section's rendered top
     at y:48, exactly below the topline, and both cell heights shrink by
     the same 48px so the bottom still lands flush on the viewport edge -
     the R6 §3 gap this block fixed doesn't reopen, because now BOTH the
     offset and the height account for the topline, not just the height. */
  .showcase-embed-cell{height:calc(100svh - 48px);}
  .showcase-side{height:calc(100svh - 48px);overflow-y:auto;}
}
.showcase-side{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;}
.showcase-panel{display:contents;}
.showcase-head{padding:calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4) var(--cellpad);}
.showcase-head .headline-40{margin-bottom:8px;}

/* R7 §C: the accordion ledger (R6 §1/§2) is replaced on desktop by a single
   crossfading box - one background for the whole "ruta", every step
   grid-stacked in one cell and GSAP-scrubbed by the showcase pin's onUpdate
   (never a class-toggle). Mobile keeps R6's stacked-rows layout unchanged;
   only its opacity mechanism changes (measured contrast fix, see below). */
.showcase-row{padding:var(--cellpad);display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:center;}
.showcase-row h3{margin-bottom:0;}
.showcase-row p{max-width:52ch;font-size:15px;margin-top:8px;}

@media (min-width:768px){
  /* R6 runda 6 (F-019/F-022): tre celler i sidans eget rutverk (gap:1px,
     background:#000 skiner igenom som fog, varje cell sin egen bakgrund) -
     räknarcellen (auto), textcellen (auto, satt av det längsta stegets
     höjd via samma grid-area:1/1-stapling som förut) och en ny detaljcell
     (1fr, fyller resten) som visar en bild ur den valda sajten per steg.
     Den lodräta stegskalan (R3-R4) är borttagen helt - Anton (F-022):
     "Det ser ut som något ofärdigt". Tom yta löses nu med riktigt innehåll
     (en bild ur arbetet), inte med ett dekorativt streck. */
  .showcase-rows{display:grid;grid-template-rows:auto auto 1fr;gap:1px;background:#000;height:100%;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-steps{background:var(--paper);color:var(--ink);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-box-head,
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-steps{background:var(--black);color:var(--paper);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-row p{color:#bdbdbd;}
  /* räknarcellen: NN/NN överst, mintspåret under - som R3, innan R4 flyttade
     räknaren ned i den nu borttagna skalan. */
  .showcase-box-head{padding:var(--cellpad);}
  .showcase-counter{display:block;font-size:13px;margin-bottom:10px;}
  .showcase-track{position:relative;height:4px;}
  .showcase-track::before{content:'';position:absolute;top:50%;left:0;right:0;height:1px;background:#000;transform:translateY(-50%);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-track::before{background:var(--paper);opacity:.3;}
  .showcase-track-fill{position:absolute;top:0;left:0;width:100%;height:4px;background:var(--mint);transform-origin:0 50%;transform:scaleX(0);}
  .showcase-steps{display:grid;}
  /* R3 §4 (F-019): rubriken får aldrig ta över - sajten är huvudsaken,
     rutan är bildtexten. h3 tillbaka i rubrikskala (30px), inte
     headline-40-tokenet R2 lånade; jättesiffran är borttagen. */
  .showcase-row{grid-area:1/1;padding:0 var(--cellpad) calc(var(--cellpad)*1.4);}
  .showcase-row h3{font-size:30px;line-height:1.15;font-weight:500;}
  .showcase-row p{font-size:18px;line-height:1.5;max-width:40ch;}
  /* detaljcellen: en <figure> per steg, grid-stackad (samma grid-area:1/1-
     teknik som .showcase-row ovan), färglager under och ett dither-rutnät
     ovanpå (buildTileGrid, samma mekanism som #kontakt/tes-bilden) som
     löses upp i den skrubbade pin-tidslinjen (C.tl, se buildStepTimelines).
     Calyx grå grund (dither svart-på-grått), Hōrai svart grund (dither
     vitt-på-svart) - samma två grundfärger dither.py redan producerar. */
  /* R6b: bilden är ett förstoringsglas (2,5-3x iframen) tagen i exakt cellens
     proportion vid 1440x900 (599,6/426,5 = 1,4058). Vid andra fönster varierar
     cellen från 0,63 (2560x1440) till 1,59 (1280x800); figuren låses därför
     till bildens proportion och passas in (contain) med container-enheter, så
     att färglagret och rutnätet ovanpå alltid täcker samma yta. Med cover
     klipptes luppen (adressen, priset) och rutorna gled ur linje mot färgen. */
  .showcase-detail{position:relative;overflow:hidden;min-height:0;container-type:size;}
  .showcase-panel--calyx .showcase-detail{background:var(--grey);}
  .showcase-panel--horai .showcase-detail{background:var(--black);}
  .showcase-figure{position:absolute;left:50%;top:50%;translate:-50% -50%;width:min(100cqw,140.58cqh);height:min(100cqh,71.13cqw);margin:0;opacity:0;}
  .showcase-figure:first-child{opacity:1;}
  .showcase-figure img{position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;object-fit:fill;}
}
@media (max-width:767px){
  /* R7 runda 2, fynd 2: .showcase-embed-cell (position:sticky) satt över
     .showcase-side (head + rader) i normalt dokumentflöde, så när huvudet
     ("Hōrai") rullade upp genom den redan-klistrade ramen (z-index:2) klipptes

     synligt INNAN raderna - och innan ramen - börjar klistra, så .showcase-side
     görs display:contents här (bara mobil) för att lyfta .showcase-head och
     .showcase-rows till .showcase-stage's egna grid-items, och ordnas om med
     `order`: huvud (1) -> ram (2, där klistringen börjar) -> rader (3). */

  .showcase-head{order:1;}
  .showcase-embed-cell{order:2;}
  .showcase-rows{display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:1px;background:#000;order:3;}

     (shots/r6-mobile-before, före denna runda): den borttagna stegskalan
     (.showcase-scale) hade ALDRIG en egen mobilregel, så dess räknartext
     redan föll igenom osynligt formaterad, som en enkel textrad i
     .showcase-rows egen svarta gap-bakgrund, ovanpå .showcase-embed-cell.
